belief: Enjoying life is worldly or sinful.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that enjoying life is worldly or sinful, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A strict religious upbringing that frowned on fun, laughter, music, or celebration. Hearing that pleasure leads to sin. Feeling guilty when relaxing or having a good time. Seeing Christianity as mostly about rules and sacrifice. Confusing worldliness with enjoyment of God’s good gifts.
teaches: God richly provides everything for us to enjoy. Ecclesiastes says there is nothing better than to rejoice, eat, drink, and find satisfaction in our work, because it is God’s gift. Jesus came that we might have life in all its fullness, and in God’s presence there is joy and eternal pleasure. Worldliness is loving the things of the world more than God, not enjoying God’s gifts with thanks.
self_statements: If I enjoy something, I should feel guilty.
Real Christians are serious all the time.
God wants me to be miserable to stay holy.
errors: Believing every pleasure is either sinful or spiritual.
“I should not enjoy life too much.”
Overlooking Scripture’s celebration of joy, feasts, and gifts.
questions: What does 1 Timothy 6:17 say God provides things for?
Did Jesus attend celebrations and feasts?
What is the difference between enjoying a gift and worshiping it?
Who taught me that enjoyment is sinful?
Does misery make me more like Christ?
What gifts has God given me to enjoy?
How could I enjoy life in a way that honors God?
truth: Enjoying life is not worldly or sinful. God richly provides everything for me to enjoy. Jesus came to give me life in all its fullness. I can enjoy God’s good gifts with thanksgiving, without making them my god. The joy of the LORD is my strength.
hw_questions: What does God provide things for?
Enjoying a gift or worshiping it: which is this?
Who taught me enjoyment is sinful?
Does misery make me more like Christ?
What gifts has God given me to enjoy?
hw_truths: God richly provides all things for me to enjoy.
Jesus came to give me life in all its fullness.
I can enjoy God’s gifts with thanksgiving.
The joy of the LORD is my strength.
In God’s presence there is fullness of joy.
Enjoyment is not the same as worldliness.
log: Each day, write one good gift I enjoyed and a one-line thank-you to God.
name_example: You have made known to Sarah the path of life; You will fill her with joy in Your presence, with eternal pleasures at Your right hand.
actions: Plan one enjoyable activity this week,
such as a meal with friends, music, or time outdoors, and thank God during it.
and write what Jesus’ first miracle says about celebration.
and thank God for the gift of humor.
tracker: One gift I enjoyed with thanks
prayer: Father, thank You for the many good gifts You give me to enjoy. Help me reject the lie that enjoying life is worldly or sinful. Teach me to receive Your gifts with thanksgiving, to keep You first, and to know that the joy of the LORD is my strength. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
